claim: 2D CAD pattern-making systems rely on parametric design and grading rules whose constraints depend heavily on the patternmaker's individual experience and are case-sensitive because garments are more flexible than other industrial products.
stance_target: patternmaking and grading in 2D CAD require subjective, experience-dependent adjustments by the modelista
scope_conditions: 2D CAD apparel patternmaking and grading systems
quoted_support: The pattern-making techniques in 2D CAD systems mainly consist of two parts: (1) individual pattern generation based on parametric design; (2) individual pattern altering based on grading rules. Since garment is more flexible than other industrial products, the constraint types used in both parametric design and the grading rules depend on pattern makers' experience which is case-sensitive [1].
entities: University Ss. Cyril and Methodius in Skopje

claim: Although various pattern-making methods have been introduced to improve clothing fit satisfaction, it remains impossible to provide a universally optimized clothing pattern for mass production using traditional 2D methods alone.
stance_target: persistent fit and grading challenges faced by patternmakers in mass apparel production
quoted_support: Fit is one of the major concerns for the clothing industry, and pattern development process is significant during clothing manufacturing and the way clothing is constructed. Various pattern making methods have been introduced to the industry considering clothing fit satisfaction, but it is still impossible to provide the optimized clothing pattern for mass production.

claim: During apparel product development, patternmakers and designers typically rely on physical dress forms for intermediate fittings because they have consistent measurements and convenience, reserving live models for final garment fitting.
stance_target: workflow and tools used by patternmakers during prototyping and fit verification
scope_conditions: Apparel product development and prototyping workflow
quoted_support: Although final garment fitting is mainly conducted with live models, during product development patternmakers and designers usually use dress forms because they have consistent measurements and are convenient to use [4].

claim: Garment shape and distance ease allowance between body and garment depend not only on pattern construction and body measurements, but also on fabric bending, shearing, tensile deformation, overhanging factor, body movement, and styling.
stance_target: complexity of ease allowance calculation in patternmaking due to fabric mechanics and dynamic posture
scope_conditions: Patternmaking ease allowance and comfort evaluation
quoted_support: Garment shape and distance ease between body and garment depends not only on garment construction and body measurements, but also on structural and mechanical characteristics of textile materials [11-14]. According to Xu and Zhang [14], the main factors affecting the values of distance ease are bending, shearing, tensile deformation and overhanging factor of material.

claim: 3D virtual fit simulation reduces physical sample development time and saves the cost of multiple physical sample iterations by allowing patternmakers to fix patterns through quick fit simulations and real-time pattern changes prior to sewing physical prototypes.
stance_target: 3D simulation mitigates the pain point of costly, repetitive physical prototyping (peças-piloto) in patternmaking
scope_conditions: Apparel prototyping using 2D/3D CAD (Modaris and CLO 3D)
quoted_support: 3D simulation technology can reduce sample development time, and save the cost of multiple iterations of samples because the virtual fitting can help to fix the patterns through quick simulations of the fit and real-time pattern change, before making actual samples [2,17,18].

claim: When boundary lines of a 2D pattern are modified during editing, the 2D pattern cannot be mapped directly onto 3D meshes without re-triangulation and refinement, or else gaps, overlaps, distortion, and flipping occur in the cloth simulation.
stance_target: technical constraints in 2D-to-3D pattern mesh mapping when pattern contours are altered
quoted_support: However, if the boundary lines of a 2D pattern have been modified, the 2D pattern cannot be mapped directly. Otherwise, gaps and overlaps will probably occur in the meshes of the resulting fine garment.

claim: Technical designers and patternmakers can use 3D virtual simulation primarily for preliminary fit analyses to verify overall length, width, shape, tightness/looseness, and the parallelism and positioning of seamlines and hems at the start of prototyping.
stance_target: specific fit verification tasks performed by technical designers and patternmakers in 3D CAD
scope_conditions: Women's straight trousers (standard size 38, Müller pattern method) in Lectra Modaris and CLO 3D
quoted_support: This implies that technical designers can use the technology mainly for preliminary fit analyses to check major fit issues of overall length, width, and shape of the garment at the beginning of the prototyping. In addition, the tightness or looseness, length, and seamline of the garment were visible with the 3D virtual simulation technology.

claim: Trousers intended for a sitting posture cannot be adequately developed solely on a standing 3D body model because sitting alters the knee construction line position, pant length, and hip/thigh circumferences, driving fabric distortion in the hips and thighs to 120% (red strain zone) compared to 100%-114% in standing poses.
stance_target: necessity of dynamic/sitting postures in pattern fit testing to detect hip and thigh strain and add ease allowance
scope_conditions: 3D virtual fit testing of women's trousers across 4 avatar poses (standing, second standing, moving, sitting) in CLO 3D
quoted_support: It is a fact that garments for a sitting posture cannot be developed on a standing 3D body model, as there are differences in the position of the construction line of the knee, the length of the pants and the circumference of the pants around the hips and thighs, as can be seen in Figure 8. Based on that, as can be seen in Figure 8 in relation to strain maps where the greatest distortion of the pants is in the sitting position, with the appearance of red in the area of the hips and thighs, i.e. in these places there is 120% of distortion.
